programmes.d: A handsome Italian count arrives in North Fork. The town bully challenges him to a duel.
A new bank opens and Banker Hamilton hires a slow-witted gunman to guard the safe.
Mark tries to play Cupid between Lucas and a stranger who arrives in North Fork.
An arch-criminal has been run out of New Orleans and is passing through North Fork.
Young Dan Willard takes on Marshal Micah Torrence's job.
Lucas and Mark are returning from a big cattle sale when the stage is robbed by three outlaws.
Lucas suspects a nobleman, recently arrived from England, of cattle rustling.
An Argentine family moves to North Fork. The townspeople mock their clothing and customs.
Lucas and Mark find themselves exposed to anthrax when they adopt a horse.
After the Civil War, General Phil Sheridan is on an inspection tour of the New Mexico land.
Outlaws hunt a retired gunfighter who has settled in North Fork.
An old friend of Lucas McCain's, a traveling photographer, comes to North Fork plying his trade.
The townsfolk of North Fork decide to give a young couple a shivaree celebration.
When a young boy is accused of murder, Mark hides him until he can find the real killer.
A U.S. marshal arrives in North Fork, taking an Indian prisoner back east for trial.
A woman whom Lucas remembers as a card cheat opens a boardinghouse in town.
Lucas puts his life in jeopardy when he agrees to testify in a murder case.
Outlaw negotiates surrender.
Lucas welcomes his old friend, unaware that the man is now a bank robber on the run with his gang.
An old enemy of Marshal Micah Torrance's arrives in town, bent on revenge.
A marshal from another territory comes to North Fork looking for a wanted man.
Lucas comes to the rescue when escaped convicts hold up the general store in North Fork.
Young Mark manages to capture a hawk but falls into danger with a rattlesnake.
A young man wants an education despite his uncle's objection.
The McCains try to be tolerant of their embittered neighbor Abel MacDonald.
The North Fork schoolteacher is pressured to leave town because of her progressive ideas.
A hired gunman arrives in town to kill a man Lucas has hated for years.
A drought has forced local cowhands to seek work on a railroad construction project.
Lucas gives blood to save a dying man.
Mark finding a murder victim's body sets Lucas, Artemis and Marshal on a search for the killer.
A band of Indians kidnaps Mark and disappears into the hills.
An infamous train robber dies and leaves his ill-gotten wealth to Lucas.
A man dies after the bank forecloses the mortgage on his ranch; his son blames the banker for this.
A rancher is shot by an unknown killer, and his daughter's lover is jailed.
A group of outlaws devises a plan to get rid of Lucas so that they can take over North Fork.
After Lucas kills a mountain man in a brawl, his father arrives to break his other boys out of jail.
Newly arrived gunslinger Al Walker throws a mammoth party at the saloon.
Lucas accuses a reporter's misleading articles of causing an innocent man's death.
Lucas and Mark lie to protect a family.
Lucas becomes involved in the family troubles of the hotel clerk.
Fallen ill, a couple seeks shelter.
Lucas and Mark are stranded in the middle of a desert with very little food or water.
Stagecoach robbers hold Mark hostage.
Outlaws threaten to kill Micah.
Lucas tries to do a good deed for the town drunk but it backfires.
